text:
Situation: FDA first posted the hydromorphone hydrochloride injection shortage on 2017-10-31 and it remains Current as of 2026-10-21. The posting lists Fresenius Kabi USA LLC, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc., Hospira Inc. (a Pfizer Company), and Teva Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. as affected manufacturers. Our Corvale East and Corvale General sites both use the Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. 2 mg/mL 20 mL vial (NDC 00641234141). Corvale East has 2.8 days on hand of that presentation; Corvale General has 21.3 days.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 976095 of Hospira Inc. (FEI 1925262) ended 2016-06-08 with an OAI classification, 510 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to Hospira Inc. (FEI 1925262) on 2017-02-14, 259 days before the posting. FDA inspection 1031233 of Hospira Inc. (FEI 1925262) ended 2017-10-27 with a VAI classification, 4 days before the posting.

Our position: Corvale East is critically low on the 2 mg/mL 20 mL vial. Corvale General holds sufficient stock to support a transfer while maintaining a two-week supply. Alternate concentrations from Hikma and Hospira are available but require dose and volume recalculation.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 139 vials of hydromorphone hydrochloride 2 mg/mL 20 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires approval by the Pharmacy Director and a DEA Form 222 or CSOS order (Schedule II).
2. Use Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. hydromorphone hydrochloride 2 mg/mL alternate concentration or vial size — requires pharmacist verification for dose and volume recalculation; approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2025-10-13.
3. Use Hospira Inc. hydromorphone hydrochloride 1 mg/mL alternate concentration or vial size — requires pharmacist verification for dose and volume recalculation; approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2026-06-05; FDA lists this product Current (posted 2017-10-31).

Not recommended: No other actions at this time.
